name: Chao hau
summary: Cháo hàu is rice porridge with oysters, fried shallots, cilantro, and fish sauce. It is the soft bowl after a day out.
origin: Vung Tau, the soft bowl after a day out.
howToEat: Eat it from the bowl, with the fried shallots and cilantro.

In Dong Hoi, Nhật Lệ oysters are shelled, rinsed, and stir-fried with scallion, chili, pepper, salt, and fish sauce, then added to rice porridge, with bone broth optional. A second way drops the seasoned raw oyster into boiling porridge. Herbs, or chili in shrimp-paste fish sauce, finish the bowl. Spring, around Tết, is the season; from July through November the oysters are fewer and less good.
where: In Dong Hoi the oysters come from the Nhật Lệ. The bowl is at Quán Hàu, about 7 km south of the center on National Highway 1A, in Lương Ninh–Quán Hàu, a white porridge finished with pepper and scallion.
seoTitle: Chao hau — oyster porridge in Vung Tau
seoDescription: Cháo hàu is oyster rice porridge with fried shallots, cilantro, and fish sauce, the soft bowl after a day out in Vung Tau.
